title: Matplotlib Scatter Plots
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and main concepts of Matplotlib Scatter Plots.
Create a Matplotlib Figure and Axes suitable for the visualization task.
Apply the relevant plotting API and configure its key properties.
Inspect plotted artists or chart properties to verify the intended result.
Choose labels and visual encodings that communicate data accurately.
prerequisites: NumPy arrays and basic numeric data

understand.concept: A scatter plot displays paired numeric observations as points. The scatter method accepts x and y arrays and can encode additional variables through color, size and transparency. Arrays must align so each observation is represented correctly.
understand.whyItMatters: Scatter plots help inspect relationships, clusters and unusual observations between two numeric variables.
understand.analogy: Each point is a pin on a map where one measurement sets the horizontal position and another sets the vertical position.
understand.summary: Matplotlib Scatter Plots is part of the Matplotlib learning path. The examples use deterministic data and the Agg backend for automated execution.

explain.narrative: Read the concept, execute each example in sequence, inspect the printed result and compare it with the expected output. Each example creates a figure with the non-interactive Agg backend and closes it after inspection.

examples.title: Create a scatter plot
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
points = ax.scatter([1, 2], [3, 4])
print(points.get_offsets().shape)
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: Two x-y pairs create two two-dimensional offsets.

examples.title: Count plotted observations
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
points = ax.scatter([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6])
print(len(points.get_offsets()))
plt.close(fig)

examples.title: Set point sizes
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
points = ax.scatter([1, 2], [3, 4], s=100)
print(int(points.get_sizes()[0]))
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: The s argument controls marker area.

examples.title: Encode values with color
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
points = ax.scatter([1, 2], [3, 4], c=[10, 20], cmap='viridis')
print(points.get_array().tolist())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: The c array maps observations to colormap values.

examples.title: Adjust point transparency
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
points = ax.scatter([1, 2], [3, 4], alpha=0.5)
print(points.get_alpha())
plt.close(fig)

practise.independentTask: Apply the technique to a small dataset of your own. Include meaningful labels, check input lengths and explain why the chosen chart is appropriate.

Create the Figure and Axes explicitly with plt.subplots().
